data.name: Kajji
data.gender_notes: Kajji is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'kajj', meaning 'pure' or 'clear'. This name is often given to babies born during the holy month of Ramadan. The name Kajji carries the meaning “Pure, Clear” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Kajji usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the purity of the soul and the clarity of the mind. It is a reminder to live a life free from worldly distractions and material possessions.
data.etymology: Kajji belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Clear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kajji total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: كاجي
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من كاج، يعني مائل أو منحرف
in_arabic.long_meaning: الكاجي هو اسم مشتق من كاج، والذي يعني مائل أو منحرف. وقد ورد في بعض التفاسير أن الكاجي يعني الشخص الذي يميل إلى الحق أو الباطل. وقد استخدم هذا الاسم في بعض الأوقات لوصف الشخص الذي يتبع نهجًا وسطًا في حياته.

in_urdu.name: کاجی
in_urdu.meaning: کاگ سے ماخوذ، مطلب ہے مائل یا منحرف
in_urdu.long_meaning: کاجی ایک ایسا نام ہے جو کاگ سے ماخوذ ہے، جو مائل یا منحرف کے معنی میں ہے۔ یہ نام بعض اوقات ایسے شخص کی وضاحت کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جو زندگی میں ایک متوازن انداز اپناتا ہے۔ اس کا تعلق عربی جڑوں سے ہے اور اسلامی ثقافت میں اس کا استعمال ملتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: काजी
in_hindi.meaning: काग से लिया गया, अर्थ है झुका हुआ या टेढ़ा
in_hindi.long_meaning: काजी नाम काग से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है झुका हुआ या टेढ़ा। यह नाम उन व्यक्तियों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो जीवन में संतुलित दृष्टिकोण रखते हैं। इसकी जड़ें अरबी भाषा में हैं और यह इस्लामी संस्कृति में प्रयोग होता है।

in_pashto.name: کاجی
in_pashto.meaning: د کاج څخه اخیستل شوی، مانا یې مائل یا منحرف
in_pashto.long_meaning: کاجی نوم د کاج څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې مانا یې مائل یا منحرف دی. دا نوم د هغو کسانو د بیان لپاره کارول کیږي چې په ژوند کې توازن لرونکی لار تعقیبوي. دا نوم عربي ريښې لري او په اسلامي کلتور کې يې کارول موندل کيږي.

While there isn't a direct Quranic reference, the name's usage is embedded in Islamic tradition and culture, signifying a person with a moderate or middle path in life.

Naming a child Kajji during Ramadan is seen as an auspicious tradition, symbolizing the purity and clarity of the soul, and the cleansing nature of the holy month. This practice emphasizes the importance of moral rectitude and spiritual growth in Islamic society.

It represents the quest for purity of the soul and the desire to lead a virtuous life in accordance with Islamic teachings. By bestowing this name upon a child, parents are instilling a fundamental Islamic value and highlighting their faith in the transformative power of spiritual practices. The name Kajji serves as a constant reminder of the importance of striving towards inner purification and maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah.

Ain-i-Akbari, 1590 AD
Kajji is mentioned as a revered Sufi saint of Multan, Pakistan.
Context: Abul Fazl, the author of Ain-i-Akbari, wrote about various Sufi saints in India. Kajji was one of them, known for his piety and miracles.
